chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa (peace be upon him): 'What should I do if I intend to perform Tamattu'?' He said: 'Recite the Talbiyah for Hajj and intend the Tamattu'. When you enter Mecca, perform Tawaf around the House, pray two Rak'ahs behind the Maqam, perform Sa'i between al-Safa and al-Marwah, and perform Qasr (shortening of prayer), then annul the Ihram of Umrah and make it Tamattu'.

key_terms.التَّمَتُّع: Tamattu' (a type of Hajj where Umrah and Hajj are performed separately with a break in Ihram)
key_terms.القَصْر: Qasr (shortening the four-rak'ah prayer to two rak'ahs while traveling)
key_terms.فَسْخ: Faskh (annulment or release from the state of Ihram)

ai.seo_question: How does one perform the rituals of Hajj al-Tamattu' according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam Ali ibn Musa (al-Rida) clarifies the procedural mechanics of Hajj al-Tamattu', emphasizing that the pilgrim must explicitly intend the transition from Umrah to Hajj while in Mecca. The instruction to 'shorten' (qasr) the Umrah rites signifies the dissolution of the Umrah Ihram, allowing the pilgrim to re-enter Ihram for Hajj later, a key distinction in Shia jurisprudence regarding the separation of the two pilgrimages.
